subject: crab
pitch: A feisty red rock crab with one oversized claw raised in challenge. A wide, knobbly shell in brick red speckled with orange and cream, eyes on stalks, eight jointed walking legs with pointed tips, and claws with dark tips and little teeth on the pinchers. A tiny barnacle and a strand of seaweed cling to the back of its shell.
reasoning:
I'm planning out the crab model's structure efficiently—sizing the carapace, positioning the root body joint, and sketching the leg skeleton with coxa-based chains for IK to ground contact points.

For the legs, I'm defining joint chains per side with hip, knee, ankle, and foot points to form articulated limbs. For the shell, I'm shaping it as a scaled, flattened sphere with low-poly detail and mottled coloring, then planning to scatter small knobs across its surface.

Now I'm adding eye stalks as thin rods topped with spheres for the eyes, plus separate jaw and mouthpart pieces, and starting to lay out a raised claw arm with shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints.

Designing the pincer hand with a fixed finger and a jointed dactyl using curved sweeps for the claw shape, plus small tooth spikes along the inner edge, and planning a reusable claw-building function based on a palm position and forward direction.

Building the claw hand geometry...

Still working out the pincer geometry...

I'm also figuring out which side holds the big claw versus the small claw, orienting each wrist and finger direction differently so the big claw opens horizontally on the left while the small claw sits lowered and angled forward on the right.

Now I'm setting up the arm chains from shoulder to elbow to wrist for each side, with tapered sweep radii for the big and small arms, then moving to the legs with pointed tapered tips and darker color bands near the ends.

For the four legs, I'm working out their hip, knee, ankle, and tip positions relative to the body surface, offsetting front legs forward and back legs backward along z, with tapering radii down to a sharp point at each tip.

Now I'm sizing the overall shell dimensions and checking proportions—wide crab shell around 0.34 across with legs spanning roughly 0.62 total plus claws, aiming for a height around 0.32 at the claw tip. I'm also planning a flatter cream underbelly plate and adding small spike details along the front edge of the carapace to give it that rock crab texture.

For surface details, I'm scattering small cream and orange knobs across the shell using a raycast-based placement system with minimum distance spacing, filtered to the upper surface, then placing a barnacle shape near the back by raycasting straight down onto the shell.

For seaweed, I'm sweeping a few drooping bezier strands up from a hit point using a flat ribbon cross-section, colored dark green, to simulate kelp trailing over the back of the shell.

For the eyes, I'm setting up a two-joint stalk hierarchy per eye with a rod connecting the base to a small cream-and-black eye sphere at the tip, built as bones so they can articulate.

Now I'm designing the mouth with a jaw joint for pivoting, an upper maxilla box part fixed to the body, and a lower jaw box part attached to the jaw bone, positioning everything so it aligns with the shell's front curvature near the underside.

I'm defining the color palette and building the coat pattern layer by layer—base red/deep mottling, orange spots for texture, then cream speckles on top—reusing the same coat treatment for the legs, while setting up a pose with the big claw's dactyl slightly open.
